pages.title: MCHP Expands Ethernet Portfolio: Can it Challenge TXN & ADI?
pages.text:
Skip to navigation Skip to main content Skip to right column
MCHP Expands Ethernet Portfolio: Can it Challenge TXN & ADI?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:20 AM PDT 4 min read
Microchip Technology MCHP has expanded its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with the launch of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 PMD transceivers and the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family with integrated transceivers. The products are designed for next-generation zonal architectures across automotive, industrial, robotics and aerospace and defense applications, extending Ethernet connectivity to edge nodes while reducing wiring and system complexity. The portfolio combines transceivers, endpoint functionality, power management and embedded-control capabilities, thereby supporting MCHP's broader Total System Solutions strategy. It also improves competitive prowess against the likes of Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI.
The LAN8679 features an Open Alliance 3-Pin interface in a compact package, while the LAN8680 adds power management, wake as well as sleep control and watchdog supervision. The LAN8660X/1X/2X family integrates a transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol solution, eliminating the need for external PHY components in applications such as control systems, lighting and audio. Microchip's 10BASE-T1S multidrop architecture can connect eight or more nodes over a single bus, helping reduce wiring weight, costs and gateway requirements.
The portfolio expansion strengthens Microchip's connectivity and networking growth strategy. The company identifies connectivity/networking as one of its new strategic growth pillars, targeting opportunities across Industry 4.0, automotive and data-center applications. MCHP highlights Single Pair Ethernet as a roughly $4-billion served available market, spanning automotive, aerospace, robotics, industrial vehicles, building controls, industrial controls, sensors, actuators and vehicle networking. The company also sees billions of legacy nodes as potential replacement opportunities, giving the expanded portfolio a sizable long-term addressable market.
The launch is also well timed with improving demand in MCHP's two largest target markets for these products. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, industrial represented 32.2% of revenues and automotive accounted for 15%. Industrial revenues increased 24.3% year over year, while automotive revenues jumped 29.3%. Industrial and automotive customers had largely completed inventory corrections, and Microchip noted that clients were placing a higher number of orders, while bookings remained strong across product lines, business units and geographies. The new devices are expected to help Microchip capture more semiconductor content as automotive and industrial networks migrate from fragmented legacy architectures toward consolidated Ethernet-based systems.
Texas Instruments' DP83TD555 targets 10BASE-T1S connectivity, while ADI's AD3300/AD3301 family brings integrated Ethernet connectivity to edge sensors and actuators.
Texas Instruments is challenging Microchip across automotive and industrial connectivity through its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolio, strong manufacturing capacity and growing semiconductor content per system. In the second quarter of 2026, TXN's industrial revenues increased roughly 30% year over year, while automotive revenues rose in the mid-teens. Texas Instruments' supply capabilities further intensify the challenge. The company has available clean-room space and is expanding production capacity to address rising demand.
Analog Devices poses a significant challenge through its high-performance analog, sensing, power and embedded technologies. Microchip Technology stock (ISIN US5950171042) gained 4.98 percent to close at USD 82.41 on Nasdaq on October 2, 2026, as investors responded to the company expanding its Ethernet portfolio for automotive and industrial networks. The new devices target zonal architectures in vehicles, industrial automation, robotics and aerospace applications. Microchip says the products are designed around AEC-Q100 and ISO 26262 requirements, while the single-pair Ethernet architecture can connect multiple nodes on one bus line.
The market reaction gave the product announcement immediate financial relevance. The October 2 close was USD 3.91 above the prior close, and the session gain of 4.98 percent put the stock near the upper end of its trading range for that session.

Management's September-quarter outlook points to revenue growth of 40 percent year over year at the midpoint and a 66.5 percent gross margin, according to Investing.com. Microchip Technology Announces PAC1761 And PAC1861 Families Of 65V Energy-Aware Digital Power Monitors
Microchip Technology announced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors that combine accumulated power-measurement insights with the necessary high-voltage measurement headroom and transient spike protection capabilities to help make 48V power architectures more efficient and resilient. The move to 48V power architectures demands that digital power monitors have an additional operational margin of up-to-65V measurement and 75V of spike protection to ensure transient survivability. The PAC1761 and PAC1861 devices add to these capabilities the intelligence to understand and react in real time to energy usage dynamics based on accumulated power measurement data.
Microchip?s digital power monitoring devices feature programmable alerts for voltage, current and power excursions, step-limit detection to identify sudden load changes, and configurable accumulated-energy thresholds that enable proactive system management based on both instantaneous and long-term power behavior. Target applications include automotive, AI/data center, networking, industrial, server, telecom/Power over Ethernet (PoE) and 48V power distribution systems. The 12-bit PAC1761 and 16-bit PAC1861 options are available in VDFN-8 (similar to SOT23-8), VDFN-10 and MSOP-10 packages including automotive-orderable variants. Pin-compatible options can reduce redesign risk, shorten qualification cycles and give customers flexibility to move between devices as requirements, availability, cost or performance change.
Development support includes evaluation board EV12R33A, a Python Command Line Interface (CLI) with library, Linux® driver and generic C library with multiple MCU code examples. Products in the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families are available now starting at $0.56 each in 10,000-unit quantities for the PAC1761T-3E/E3 and PAC1861T-1E/3P, both in the MSOP-10 package. The price of the evaluation board EV12R33A is $49.00.

pages.text:
U.S. semiconductor company Microchip Technology’s Armenia operations and investment plans discussed in Yerevan - ARMENPRESS Armenian News Agency
U.S. semiconductor company Microchip Technology’s Armenia operations and investment plans discussed in Yerevan
Armenia’s Minister of High-Tech Industry and Artificial Intelligence Davit Tadevosyan received representatives of Microchip Technology, led by Shakeel Peera, Corporate Vice President of the corporation's FPGA business unit.
The Ministry said in a readout that the meeting focused on a number of issues related to the development and expansion of the company’s operations in Armenia.
The sides also discussed the company’s activities in Gyumri, Vanadzor and Ijevan, emphasizing the importance of Microchip Technology’s presence in developing the high-tech sector in the regions, attracting professional talent and strengthening local technology ecosystems.
The sides also discussed the approval of an export license obtained by the company in June 2026 from the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) for its operations in Armenia, as well as its potential impact on the company’s future activities, investment programs and development opportunities.
The meeting also addressed measures needed to ensure the necessary conditions for importing Microchip products into Armenia. In this context, the sides discussed ongoing talks between the Ministry and representatives of international semiconductor companies and the U.S. government on developing a categorized list of products.
The sides agreed to continue working to implement further steps in the areas discussed and expand cooperation.
Microchip Technology Inc. is an American semiconductor company that develops and manufactures microprocessors, FPGAs, analog and power-management solutions, as well as communications, memory and other embedded-system components. The company’s technologies are used in industry, automotive, aerospace and defense systems, communications, computing and other sectors.

pages.title: Microchip Expands Single Pair Ethernet Portfolio with New 10BASE‑T1S Devices Enabling Scalable Edge Connectivity
pages.text:
Skip to navigation Skip to main content Skip to right column
This is a paid press release. Contact the press release distributor directly with any inquiries.
Microchip Expands Single Pair Ethernet Portfolio with New 10BASE‑T1S Devices Enabling Scalable Edge Connectivity
Microchip Technology Inc.
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:00 AM PDT 3 min read
Microchip Technology Inc.
New transceivers and integrated endpoint family simplify zonal architectures and reduce system complexity for automotive and industrial applications
CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announces the expansion of its 10BASE-T1S portfolio with the introduction of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 10BASE‑T1S PMD transceivers, alongside the LAN8660X/1X/2X family of endpoints with integrated transceivers. Designed to support next-generation zonal architectures, these solutions deliver flexible, space-efficient connectivity that extends Ethernet to the network edge.
As automotive, industrial and robotics systems evolve toward fully Ethernet-based networks, designers face increasing demands for simplified architectures, reduced wiring complexity and efficient edge node integration. Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S devices address these challenges and are designed to meet AEC-Q100 and ISO 26262 functional safety standards, building on Microchip's VelocityDRIVE™ portfolio with additional multidrop connectivity solutions featuring a standardized, streamlined interface.
The LAN8679 transceiver provides a standardized Open Alliance 3‑Pin (OA3P) interface in a compact 8‑pin VDFN package, supporting space-constrained edge nodes, while reducing pin count and design complexity. The LAN8680 builds on these capabilities by integrating System Basis Chip (SBC) features, including power management, system wake/sleep control and watchdog supervision. Both devices are engineered to enhance reliability and safety for demanding environments such as automotive and industrial applications.
"Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S portfolio advances our commitment to enabling scalable, all‑Ethernet network architectures," said Charlie Forni, corporate vice president of Microchip's networking and connectivity business unit. "By combining OA3P interface simplicity with integrated endpoint functionality, these devices give designers the flexibility to build efficient, reliable systems while significantly reducing complexity at the edge."
Complementing these devices, the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family integrates a PMD transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol (RCP) solution. This approach enables designers to deploy compact, fully integrated edge nodes for applications such as control systems, lighting and audio without the need for external PHY components.
By leveraging 10BASE‑T1S multidrop topology, Microchip's solutions allow multiple nodes—typically eight or more—to share a single bus line. This reduces wiring weight, lowers system costs and eliminates the need for gateways, making it easier to connect sensors and actuators directly to the network edge.
Microchip's expanded Single Pair Ethernet portfolio targets a wide range of applications, including automotive zonal architecture, industrial automation, robotics and aerospace and defense systems. The products align with industry trends toward consolidated networks and simplified connectivity frameworks, enabling designers to implement efficient and scalable all-Ethernet architectures. For more information about Microchip's Single Pair Ethernet solutions, visit the website.
The LAN8679, LAN8680 and LAN8660X/1X/2X are available in limited sampling. To learn more, please contact a Microchip sales representative.

Microchip Technology stock (ISIN US5950171042) closed at USD 71.48 on the Nasdaq on September 14, 2026, down 3.7 percent on the day as investors reassessed both valuation and the latest guidance from the semiconductor manufacturer.
According to MarketBeat data cited in a recent news overview, Microchip Technology stock finished the September 14, 2026 session at USD 71.48 on its primary Nasdaq listing, after a 3.7 percent decline from the prior close as chip shares softened.
A separate valuation analysis from GuruFocus on September 14, 2026 noted that Microchip Technology shares closed at USD 71.48, while its GF Value fair-value estimate stood at USD 66.03, implying the stock was approximately 8.3 percent overvalued at that level.
The same analysis highlighted a 52-week trading range between USD 48.52 and USD 105.91, placing the September 14, 2026 close closer to the lower half of that band and underscoring how far the stock remains below its highs despite the year-to-date gain.
Quarterly figures show improving margins but cautious outlook
Recent corporate-news coverage summarized Microchip Technology's latest quarterly results, reporting revenue of USD 462.1 million for the most recent quarter, which was up 13.9 percent versus the preceding quarter and 3.3 percent year on year, signaling a gradual recovery from the prior downturn.
In the same report, operating loss for the quarter was given as USD 7.17 million, a reduction of 42.4 percent compared with the prior quarter, indicating that cost measures and mix effects are beginning to narrow losses even as demand normalizes.
The company also reported a gross margin of 15.6 percent for the quarter, at the upper half of its guidance range of 14.0 to 16.0 percent, which suggests that the business is managing pricing and cost pressures better than initially feared.
However, forward-looking guidance remained cautious: Microchip Technology guided revenue for the following quarter to a range of USD 445.0 million to USD 485.0 million and indicated an expected gross margin between 17 and 19 percent, combining a slightly wider margin outlook with a revenue range that does not point to a sharp rebound.
According to a recent article on Yahoo Finance on September 14, 2026, Microchip Technology stock is up about 15 percent year to date as the company climbs out of a deep inventory correction, but peers such as Texas Instruments have captured share by ramping capacity earlier in the cycle.
That mix of improving quarterly margins, still-modest revenue growth and a cautious demand backdrop helps explain why the shares have retreated from higher levels even as the fundamental picture has stopped deteriorating.
Analyst consensus points to upside from current levels
Analyst data compiled by MarketBeat show that Microchip Technology currently carries an average rating score of 2.79 based on 3 strong buy ratings, 13 buy ratings and 8 hold ratings, with no sell recommendations as of mid-September 2026.
The same overview lists a consensus price target of USD 98.67, representing roughly 38.0 percent upside from a reference price around USD 71.51, indicating that the analyst community still sees room for appreciation if the cyclical recovery in microcontrollers and related product lines continues.
For investors, the tension between valuation metrics such as the GF Value estimate of USD 66.03 and the consensus target near USD 98.67 is a central point: the current price sits about 8.3 percent above one fair-value model yet more than 25 percent below where analysts expect the shares to trade over the medium term.
Year-to-date performance adds another layer to that picture: MarketBeat data indicate the stock started 2026 at USD 63.72 and has since risen to roughly USD 71.51, an increase of around 12.2 percent, which is solid but not spectacular compared with some faster-moving peers in the semiconductor space.
Inventory correction and peer dynamics shape the risk profile
The broader sector context also matters for Microchip Technology stock. As the Yahoo Finance article on September 14, 2026 highlighted, Microchip Technology has been working through a deep inventory correction, while Texas Instruments installed clean-room capacity ahead of the upturn and may have captured incremental share during the normalization phase.
This dynamic suggests that Microchip Technology's recovery in revenue and margins could be more gradual than that of some competitors, leaving the company more exposed if macro or end-market demand softens again.
On the other hand, improving gross margins and a shrinking operating loss indicate that management is using the correction to tighten cost structures and refine product and customer mix, which could position the company to benefit when demand accelerates more broadly.
Analyst consensus ratings that skew toward buy rather than hold or sell reflect a view that, despite near-term caution and valuation questions, the long-term secular drivers in embedded control, automotive, industrial and other end markets remain intact.
Stock trades below the midpoint of its 52-week range
Per Nasdaq-based pricing cited in recent coverage, Microchip Technology stock closed at USD 71.48 on Nasdaq on September 14, 2026, with the shares trading within a 52-week range of USD 48.52 to USD 105.91 and remaining well below the highs reached earlier in the cycle.
At the USD 71.48 close, the stock stood about USD 22.96 above the 52-week low but USD 34.43 below the 52-week high, placing it nearer to the lower half of the range and illustrating how much headroom remains if fundamentals and sentiment improve.

MCHP Expands 48V Power Portfolio: Can It Outpace TXN & ADI?
Microchip Technology MCHP is strengthening its position in power management as demand for efficient power delivery and monitoring rises across Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centers, automotive, industrial and communications applications. The company's analog portfolio spans power management, high-voltage products, thermal management, MOSFETs, gate drivers and mixed-signal solutions. This broad portfolio supports MCHP's Total System Solution strategy across microcontrollers, microprocessors, analog, FPGA, memory and connectivity products, while helping it compete with Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI in power management applications. MCHP also identifies AI/ML, data centers, edge computing, networking and connectivity as key growth areas.
Building on this foundation, Microchip Technology introduced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors for 48V architectures. The devices measure voltage, current, power and accumulated energy while offering transient protection, helping improve power efficiency, system reliability and energy visibility. The launch broadens MCHP's exposure to applications such as AI servers, networking equipment, automotive systems and industrial infrastructure. The company already targets power supplies, smart meters and energy monitoring, storage and server systems, and scale-up and scale-across AI infrastructure.
The expansion is particularly relevant to MCHP's growing data-center business. Data centers represented 17.1% of first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues, while data-center sales surged 97.8% year over year. Management said its data-center exposure spans power-management analog products, mixed-signal products, microcontrollers, security products, FPGAs, timing, memory, PCIe switches and storage controllers. MCHP revenues from catalog products sold into data centers are expected to increase from about $288 million in calendar 2025 to roughly $500 million in 2026. Including the Data Center Solutions business, MCHP expects total data-center revenues of about $1 billion in 2026, up roughly 69% year over year.
Management expects design wins across power management, mixed-signal, storage, security and connectivity products to support further data-center growth in 2027 and beyond. MCHP's catalog products are often designed into systems through power-supply manufacturers, module makers and card suppliers, giving the company indirect exposure to hyperscaler infrastructure deployments.
Texas Instruments is intensifying competition with MCHP through its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolios. TXN highlighted that data-center revenues doubled year over year in the second quarter of 2026. Management also highlighted the transition toward 800V architectures, where power could move through stages such as 800V-to-48V and 48V-to-12V. This creates more conversion points and expands opportunities for TXN's analog, embedded-control and signal-chain products.
Analog Devices is challenging MCHP through a broader grid-to-chip power strategy spanning energy infrastructure, rack power and processor-level delivery. ADI said customers are using its solutions to achieve more than 98% conversion efficiency, multi-kilowatt power delivery, protection, telemetry and fault recording. Its 800V-to-intermediate conversion technologies can deliver 20 kilowatts at power densities above 2.5 kilowatts per cubic inch. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, ADI also said data-center power revenues grew more than 100% year over year, while its Empower acquisition extends power delivery into the processor package, intensifying competition as AI infrastructure shifts toward higher-voltage, higher-density power architectures.

ADI vs. MCHP: Which Semiconductor Stock Has an Upside Now?
Analog Devices ADI and Microchip Technology MCHP are two of the largest semiconductor players catering to industrial, automotive, communications, consumer and data center end markets, making their businesses quite diversified. With the recent boom in the semiconductor industry, the question remains: which stock has more upside potential? Let us break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which offers a more compelling investment case.
Analog Devices delivered a strong fiscal third-quarter 2026 result, with revenues rising 40% year over year to $4.02 billion, supported by growth across all end markets. ADI's adjusted operating margin expanded to 50%, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) jumped 68% to $3.45. Analog Devices expects fourth-quarter revenues of $4.3 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.86 at the midpoint. Broad-based demand, improving profitability and stronger guidance indicate that ADI's recovery could extend across multiple quarters.
ADI's industrial business contributed 49% of revenue, which grew 53% year over year and 10% sequentially to $1.97 billion. The growth in this segment was primarily led by automated test equipment, electronic test and measurement, aerospace and defense, and automation. ADI sees longer-term opportunities from factory automation, robotics and physical AI, where increasing sensing, motion-control, power and connectivity requirements can expand semiconductor content.
Analog Devices' communications revenues surged 84% year over year and 18% sequentially to $654.5 million, with data centers accounting for roughly 80% of the segment. ADI's optical and power revenue each grew more than 100% year over year, highlighting strong AI infrastructure demand. Management expects continued data-center strength, while the Empower Semiconductor acquisition expands ADI's power-management capabilities. ADI expects its optical circuit switching revenues to roughly double in fiscal 2026.
ADI's automotive revenues increased 16% year over year and 14% sequentially to $998.2 million, supported by ADAS, infotainment and electric powertrains. Its hybrid manufacturing model is also improving supply flexibility as demand strengthens. Meanwhile, ADI generated $4.9 billion of free cash flow over the trailing 12 months and returned $5.17 billion to shareholders. Strong cash generation, buybacks and dividends provide additional support as industrial, automotive and AI infrastructure demand recovers.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 and 2027 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 37% and 22%, respectively. The consensus mark for EPS suggests a robust year-over-year improvement of 66% for fiscal 2026 and 25% for fiscal 2027. The earnings estimates for ADI's fiscal 2026 have been revised upward in the past 60 days.
Microchip is expanding its data-center portfolio as AI infrastructure drives demand for high-speed connectivity and embedded control. PCIe Gen6 design wins reached 14 by September 2026, while the company expects its data-center portfolio to generate about $1 billion in calendar 2026 revenues. Future Gen6 switch and retimer contributions could provide an additional growth catalyst from 2027 onward.
Aerospace and defense remains another important growth avenue, representing 16.7% of June-quarter revenues. Microchip's business has expanded from roughly $600 million in 2022 to approximately $1 billion, supported by defense inventory rebuilding and multiyear demand. Its radiation-tolerant, radiation-hardened and FPGA products address space and defense applications requiring high reliability, long lifecycles and stringent performance requirements.
Improving bookings, factory utilization and expense discipline are supporting operating leverage as Microchip's recovery progresses. Management reported its strongest bookings quarter in roughly four years and expects fiscal second-quarter 2027 gross margins of 66-67% and operating margins of 38.5-39.5%. The pending Hailo acquisition could accelerate Microchip's edge-AI roadmap while adding complementary technology and engineering capabilities.
However, external manufacturing dependence, China exposure and elevated leverage remain important risks. Microchip sources approximately 65% of wafers externally, creating potential bottlenecks if AI-driven demand tightens foundry and assembly capacity. China represents roughly 17-18% of revenue and faces increasing local competition. Meanwhile, net debt was 2.85 times adjusted EBITDA, limiting flexibility for buybacks and larger acquisitions.
For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Microchip expects net sales between $1.589 billion and $1.618 billion, which suggests sequential growth of 7-9%, with the midpoint implying approximately 40.6% year-over-year growth. The company expects non-GAAP earnings of 91-95 cents per share. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MCHP's second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 162.8%. Estimates have remained unchanged for the past 30 days.
ADI vs. MCHP: Price Performance and Valuation
Year to date, MCHP shares have climbed 17.3% compared with the 41.1% rise in ADI shares.
On the valuation front, MCHP trades at a P/S multiple of 5.85X, lower than its median of 6.95X. ADI trades at a forward 12-month P/S multiple of 10.22X, lower than its median of 11.22X.
ADI has the stronger overall growth profile, supported by a broader recovery across industrial, automotive and communications markets, accelerating AI infrastructure demand and stronger upward revisions to earnings estimates. While MCHP offers significant recovery potential, its higher external manufacturing dependence, China exposure and leverage create additional execution risks. Given the factors, ADI seems to be a better investment choice at present. ADI carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), while MCHP has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) at present. Microchip Technology (MCHP) Has Investors Asking A New Question
Microchip Technology (MCHP) has launched its PAC1761 and PAC1861 digital power monitor families, a product update that draws attention to how the stock reflects the company's exposure to 48V power architectures.
Recent trading shows how fast sentiment around Microchip Technology can shift. The share price has fallen 15.06% over the past 90 days despite a 14.85% year-to-date share price return, while total shareholder return over five years of 8.54% points to more modest long-run progress.
Seize this pullback in Microchip Technology to review how other chip-related plays with resilient power or AI exposure are setting up in the 84 AI infrastructure stocks.
Bulls see a resilient embedded franchise and fresh 48V and AI hooks, while bears point to the recent 15% slide and cyclical risks. Which story does Microchip Technology's current pricing actually support?
On the most followed view, Microchip Technology's fair value sits at $108.64 against a last close of $74.69, which puts the recent pullback in a very different light and shifts the focus to how emerging AI and aerospace demand might feed into future results.
Microchip Technology is seeing structural expansion in data center and AI infrastructure exposure, with total data center revenue expected to increase from about US$591 million in 2025 to roughly US$1 billion in 2026 and PCIe Gen6 design wins, including an estimated US$100 million annual program starting in 2027, which together point to a larger contribution to future revenue.
See why 53 investors see Microchip Technology as 31% undervalued.
The most widely followed narrative rests on a discount rate of 11.88%, which is used to bring those future cash flows back to today's dollars and arrive at the $108.64 figure. That view leans on growing contributions from data center, AI, and aerospace and defense programs, as well as the current non GAAP gross margin profile and planned capital expenditure.
For investors weighing Microchip Technology after a 90 day slide of 15.06%, the gap between the $74.69 share price and the $108.64 narrative fair value highlights how much faith the market is placing on these end market trends versus the risks flagged around inventories, underutilization charges and external capacity constraints.
Result: Fair Value of $108.64 (UNDERVALUED)
Still, Microchip Technology's elevated inventories and ongoing underutilization charges, along with external foundry and packaging constraints, could quickly undermine the view that the stock is currently undervalued.

Another View: Microchip Technology Looks Expensive On Earnings
The fair value narrative presents Microchip Technology as 31% undervalued at $108.64, yet the current P/E of 110.5x tells a very different story. The stock trades well above the US Semiconductor industry on 47.3x and above peer averages on 67.5x, while the fair ratio sits at 35.7x. That gap points to valuation risk if sentiment shifts back toward those lower benchmarks, so which anchor do you trust when pricing Microchip's AI and aerospace ambitions?

pages.text:

Build Smarter, More Resilient 48V Power Systems with Energy-Aware Digital Power Monitoring from Microchip
Microchip Technology Inc.
Microchip Technology Inc.
New 65V digital power monitors help designers track accumulated energy data to improve system response in applications that also depend on higher levels of measurement headroom and spike protection
CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As automotive, AI/data center, networking and industrial systems quickly migrate toward 48V power architectures to improve efficiency and support higher power demands, designers need more than visibility into instantaneous voltage and current conditions. They need systems that understand energy use over time and can respond intelligently to changing power conditions. Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors that combine accumulated power-measurement insights with the necessary high-voltage measurement headroom and transient spike protection capabilities to help make 48V power architectures more efficient and resilient.
The move to 48V power architectures demands that digital power monitors have an additional operational margin of up-to-65V measurement and 75V of spike protection to ensure transient survivability. The PAC1761 and PAC1861 devices add to these capabilities the intelligence to understand and react in real time to energy usage dynamics based on accumulated power measurement data.
"The industry conversation is shifting from measuring power at a single point in time to understanding and responding to energy behavior across an entire system and its lifecycle," said Keith Pazul, vice president of Microchip's mixed-signal linear business unit. "The PAC1761 and PAC1861 families are designed to help customers build better performing and more reliable 48V systems that can measure instantaneous conditions and understand energy consumption and availability over time. These scalable, low-power solutions reduce monitoring overhead and include pin-compatible package options that improve source flexibility while reducing design risk."
Microchip's digital power monitoring devices feature programmable alerts for voltage, current and power excursions, step-limit detection to identify sudden load changes, and configurable accumulated-energy thresholds that enable proactive system management based on both instantaneous and long-term power behavior.
Target applications include automotive, AI/data center, networking, industrial, server, telecom/Power over Ethernet (PoE) and 48V power distribution systems. The 12-bit PAC1761 and 16-bit PAC1861 options are available in VDFN-8 (similar to SOT23-8), VDFN-10 and MSOP-10 packages including automotive-orderable variants. Pin-compatible options can reduce redesign risk, shorten qualification cycles and give customers flexibility to move between devices as requirements, availability, cost or performance change.
Development support includes evaluation board EV12R33A, a Python Command Line Interface (CLI) with library, Linux® driver and generic C library with multiple MCU code examples.
Products in the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families are available now starting at $0.56 each in 10,000-unit quantities for the PAC1761T-3E/E3 and PAC1861T-1E/3P, both in the MSOP-10 package. The price of the evaluation board EV12R33A is $49.00. You can purchase directly from Microchip or contact a Microchip sales representative or authorized worldwide distributor.

MCHP Expands Ethernet Portfolio: Can it Challenge TXN & ADI?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:20 AM PDT 4 min read
Microchip Technology MCHP has expanded its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with the launch of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 PMD transceivers and the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family with integrated transceivers. The products are designed for next-generation zonal architectures across automotive, industrial, robotics and aerospace and defense applications, extending Ethernet connectivity to edge nodes while reducing wiring and system complexity. The portfolio combines transceivers, endpoint functionality, power management and embedded-control capabilities, thereby supporting MCHP's broader Total System Solutions strategy. It also improves competitive prowess against the likes of Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI.
The LAN8679 features an Open Alliance 3-Pin interface in a compact package, while the LAN8680 adds power management, wake as well as sleep control and watchdog supervision. The LAN8660X/1X/2X family integrates a transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol solution, eliminating the need for external PHY components in applications such as control systems, lighting and audio. Microchip's 10BASE-T1S multidrop architecture can connect eight or more nodes over a single bus, helping reduce wiring weight, costs and gateway requirements.
The portfolio expansion strengthens Microchip's connectivity and networking growth strategy. The company identifies connectivity/networking as one of its new strategic growth pillars, targeting opportunities across Industry 4.0, automotive and data-center applications. MCHP highlights Single Pair Ethernet as a roughly $4-billion served available market, spanning automotive, aerospace, robotics, industrial vehicles, building controls, industrial controls, sensors, actuators and vehicle networking. The company also sees billions of legacy nodes as potential replacement opportunities, giving the expanded portfolio a sizable long-term addressable market.
The launch is also well timed with improving demand in MCHP's two largest target markets for these products. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, industrial represented 32.2% of revenues and automotive accounted for 15%. Industrial revenues increased 24.3% year over year, while automotive revenues jumped 29.3%. Industrial and automotive customers had largely completed inventory corrections, and Microchip noted that clients were placing a higher number of orders, while bookings remained strong across product lines, business units and geographies. The new devices are expected to help Microchip capture more semiconductor content as automotive and industrial networks migrate from fragmented legacy architectures toward consolidated Ethernet-based systems.
Texas Instruments' DP83TD555 targets 10BASE-T1S connectivity, while ADI's AD3300/AD3301 family brings integrated Ethernet connectivity to edge sensors and actuators.
Texas Instruments is challenging Microchip across automotive and industrial connectivity through its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolio, strong manufacturing capacity and growing semiconductor content per system. In the second quarter of 2026, TXN's industrial revenues increased roughly 30% year over year, while automotive revenues rose in the mid-teens. Texas Instruments' supply capabilities further intensify the challenge. The company has available clean-room space and is expanding production capacity to address rising demand.
Analog Devices poses a significant challenge through its high-performance analog, sensing, power and embedded technologies. Industrial accounted for 49% of ADI's third-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues and increased 53% year over year, led partly by automation, while automotive represented 25% of revenues and grew 16%. ADI said its higher content and share positions are driving automotive growth across next-generation ADAS, infotainment and electric powertrains. ADI is also positioning for the emergence of physical AI, including robotics and autonomous mobility.
MCHP's Share Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates

Microchip Technology Announces PAC1761 And PAC1861 Families Of 65V Energy-Aware Digital Power Monitors
Microchip Technology announced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors that combine accumulated power-measurement insights with the necessary high-voltage measurement headroom and transient spike protection capabilities to help make 48V power architectures more efficient and resilient. The move to 48V power architectures demands that digital power monitors have an additional operational margin of up-to-65V measurement and 75V of spike protection to ensure transient survivability. The PAC1761 and PAC1861 devices add to these capabilities the intelligence to understand and react in real time to energy usage dynamics based on accumulated power measurement data.
Microchip?s digital power monitoring devices feature programmable alerts for voltage, current and power excursions, step-limit detection to identify sudden load changes, and configurable accumulated-energy thresholds that enable proactive system management based on both instantaneous and long-term power behavior. Target applications include automotive, AI/data center, networking, industrial, server, telecom/Power over Ethernet (PoE) and 48V power distribution systems. The 12-bit PAC1761 and 16-bit PAC1861 options are available in VDFN-8 (similar to SOT23-8), VDFN-10 and MSOP-10 packages including automotive-orderable variants. Pin-compatible options can reduce redesign risk, shorten qualification cycles and give customers flexibility to move between devices as requirements, availability, cost or performance change.
Development support includes evaluation board EV12R33A, a Python Command Line Interface (CLI) with library, Linux® driver and generic C library with multiple MCU code examples. Products in the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families are available now starting at $0.56 each in 10,000-unit quantities for the PAC1761T-3E/E3 and PAC1861T-1E/3P, both in the MSOP-10 package. The price of the evaluation board EV12R33A is $49.00.

What Happened?
Shares of analog chipmaker Microchip Technology (NASDAQ: MCHP)
jumped 1.9% in the afternoon session after the company announced the expansion of its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with new transceivers and endpoint devices.
The expansion introduces the LAN8679 and LAN8680 physical layer transceivers alongside the LAN8660X/1X/2X family of endpoints with integrated transceivers to support zonal architectures. The new products are engineered to meet AEC-Q100 automotive qualification requirements and ISO 26262 functional safety standards while simplifying wiring and delivering flexible edge connectivity.
After the initial pop, the shares cooled down to $79.42, up 1.9% from the previous close.

As detailed in a company press release, Microchip launched the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V digital power monitors, which are specifically designed for 48V power applications to measure accumulated energy use and provide transient headroom to withstand sudden voltage spikes.
These new chips are designed to help engineers build smarter and more resilient high-voltage electronic systems, allowing commercial customers to better manage energy draw and protect sensitive equipment. By expanding its lineup of power-management products, Microchip is directly targeting the growing industrial demand for robust 48V architectures, prompting investors to continue bidding up the stock as they digest the expanded total addressable market.
Moving forward, the market is treating this product launch as a steady step in capturing higher-margin power management market share, though sustaining this momentum will depend on how quickly customers actually integrate the new chips into their upcoming hardware designs.

Microchip Expands Single Pair Ethernet Portfolio with New 10BASE‑T1S Devices Enabling Scalable Edge Connectivity
Microchip Technology Inc.
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 5:00 AM PDT 3 min read
Microchip Technology Inc.
New transceivers and integrated endpoint family simplify zonal architectures and reduce system complexity for automotive and industrial applications
CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announces the expansion of its 10BASE-T1S portfolio with the introduction of the LAN8679 and LAN8680 10BASE‑T1S PMD transceivers, alongside the LAN8660X/1X/2X family of endpoints with integrated transceivers. Designed to support next-generation zonal architectures, these solutions deliver flexible, space-efficient connectivity that extends Ethernet to the network edge.
As automotive, industrial and robotics systems evolve toward fully Ethernet-based networks, designers face increasing demands for simplified architectures, reduced wiring complexity and efficient edge node integration. Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S devices address these challenges and are designed to meet AEC-Q100 and ISO 26262 functional safety standards, building on Microchip's VelocityDRIVE™ portfolio with additional multidrop connectivity solutions featuring a standardized, streamlined interface.
The LAN8679 transceiver provides a standardized Open Alliance 3‑Pin (OA3P) interface in a compact 8‑pin VDFN package, supporting space-constrained edge nodes, while reducing pin count and design complexity. The LAN8680 builds on these capabilities by integrating System Basis Chip (SBC) features, including power management, system wake/sleep control and watchdog supervision. Both devices are engineered to enhance reliability and safety for demanding environments such as automotive and industrial applications.
"Microchip's latest 10BASE‑T1S portfolio advances our commitment to enabling scalable, all‑Ethernet network architectures," said Charlie Forni, corporate vice president of Microchip's networking and connectivity business unit. "By combining OA3P interface simplicity with integrated endpoint functionality, these devices give designers the flexibility to build efficient, reliable systems while significantly reducing complexity at the edge."
Complementing these devices, the LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family integrates a PMD transceiver into a single-chip Remote Control Protocol (RCP) solution. This approach enables designers to deploy compact, fully integrated edge nodes for applications such as control systems, lighting and audio without the need for external PHY components.
By leveraging 10BASE‑T1S multidrop topology, Microchip's solutions allow multiple nodes—typically eight or more—to share a single bus line. This reduces wiring weight, lowers system costs and eliminates the need for gateways, making it easier to connect sensors and actuators directly to the network edge.
Microchip's expanded Single Pair Ethernet portfolio targets a wide range of applications, including automotive zonal architecture, industrial automation, robotics and aerospace and defense systems. The products align with industry trends toward consolidated networks and simplified connectivity frameworks, enabling designers to implement efficient and scalable all-Ethernet architectures. For more information about Microchip's Single Pair Ethernet solutions, visit the website.
The LAN8679, LAN8680 and LAN8660X/1X/2X are available in limited sampling. To learn more, please contact a Microchip sales representative.

MCHP Expands 48V Power Portfolio: Can It Outpace TXN & ADI?
Microchip Technology MCHP is strengthening its position in power management as demand for efficient power delivery and monitoring rises across Artificial Intelligence (AI) data centers, automotive, industrial and communications applications. The company's analog portfolio spans power management, high-voltage products, thermal management, MOSFETs, gate drivers and mixed-signal solutions. This broad portfolio supports MCHP's Total System Solution strategy across microcontrollers, microprocessors, analog, FPGA, memory and connectivity products, while helping it compete with Texas Instruments TXN and Analog Devices ADI in power management applications. MCHP also identifies AI/ML, data centers, edge computing, networking and connectivity as key growth areas.
Building on this foundation, Microchip Technology introduced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors for 48V architectures. The devices measure voltage, current, power and accumulated energy while offering transient protection, helping improve power efficiency, system reliability and energy visibility. The launch broadens MCHP's exposure to applications such as AI servers, networking equipment, automotive systems and industrial infrastructure. The company already targets power supplies, smart meters and energy monitoring, storage and server systems, and scale-up and scale-across AI infrastructure.
The expansion is particularly relevant to MCHP's growing data-center business. Data centers represented 17.1% of first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues, while data-center sales surged 97.8% year over year. Management said its data-center exposure spans power-management analog products, mixed-signal products, microcontrollers, security products, FPGAs, timing, memory, PCIe switches and storage controllers. MCHP revenues from catalog products sold into data centers are expected to increase from about $288 million in calendar 2025 to roughly $500 million in 2026. Including the Data Center Solutions business, MCHP expects total data-center revenues of about $1 billion in 2026, up roughly 69% year over year.
Management expects design wins across power management, mixed-signal, storage, security and connectivity products to support further data-center growth in 2027 and beyond. MCHP's catalog products are often designed into systems through power-supply manufacturers, module makers and card suppliers, giving the company indirect exposure to hyperscaler infrastructure deployments.
Texas Instruments is intensifying competition with MCHP through its broad Analog and Embedded Processing portfolios. TXN highlighted that data-center revenues doubled year over year in the second quarter of 2026. Management also highlighted the transition toward 800V architectures, where power could move through stages such as 800V-to-48V and 48V-to-12V. This creates more conversion points and expands opportunities for TXN's analog, embedded-control and signal-chain products.
Analog Devices is challenging MCHP through a broader grid-to-chip power strategy spanning energy infrastructure, rack power and processor-level delivery. ADI said customers are using its solutions to achieve more than 98% conversion efficiency, multi-kilowatt power delivery, protection, telemetry and fault recording. Its 800V-to-intermediate conversion technologies can deliver 20 kilowatts at power densities above 2.5 kilowatts per cubic inch. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, ADI also said data-center power revenues grew more than 100% year over year, while its Empower acquisition extends power delivery into the processor package, intensifying competition as AI infrastructure shifts toward higher-voltage, higher-density power architectures.

ADI vs. MCHP: Which Semiconductor Stock Has an Upside Now?
Analog Devices ADI and Microchip Technology MCHP are two of the largest semiconductor players catering to industrial, automotive, communications, consumer and data center end markets, making their businesses quite diversified. With the recent boom in the semiconductor industry, the question remains: which stock has more upside potential? Let us break down their fundamentals, growth prospects, market challenges and valuation to determine which offers a more compelling investment case.
Analog Devices delivered a strong fiscal third-quarter 2026 result, with revenues rising 40% year over year to $4.02 billion, supported by growth across all end markets. ADI's adjusted operating margin expanded to 50%, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) jumped 68% to $3.45. Analog Devices expects fourth-quarter revenues of $4.3 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.86 at the midpoint. Broad-based demand, improving profitability and stronger guidance indicate that ADI's recovery could extend across multiple quarters.
ADI's industrial business contributed 49% of revenue, which grew 53% year over year and 10% sequentially to $1.97 billion. The growth in this segment was primarily led by automated test equipment, electronic test and measurement, aerospace and defense, and automation. ADI sees longer-term opportunities from factory automation, robotics and physical AI, where increasing sensing, motion-control, power and connectivity requirements can expand semiconductor content.
Analog Devices' communications revenues surged 84% year over year and 18% sequentially to $654.5 million, with data centers accounting for roughly 80% of the segment. ADI's optical and power revenue each grew more than 100% year over year, highlighting strong AI infrastructure demand. Management expects continued data-center strength, while the Empower Semiconductor acquisition expands ADI's power-management capabilities. ADI expects its optical circuit switching revenues to roughly double in fiscal 2026.
ADI's automotive revenues increased 16% year over year and 14% sequentially to $998.2 million, supported by ADAS, infotainment and electric powertrains. Its hybrid manufacturing model is also improving supply flexibility as demand strengthens. Meanwhile, ADI generated $4.9 billion of free cash flow over the trailing 12 months and returned $5.17 billion to shareholders. Strong cash generation, buybacks and dividends provide additional support as industrial, automotive and AI infrastructure demand recovers.
The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 and 2027 revenues indicates year-over-year growth of 37% and 22%, respectively. The consensus mark for EPS suggests a robust year-over-year improvement of 66% for fiscal 2026 and 25% for fiscal 2027. The earnings estimates for ADI's fiscal 2026 have been revised upward in the past 60 days.
Microchip is expanding its data-center portfolio as AI infrastructure drives demand for high-speed connectivity and embedded control. PCIe Gen6 design wins reached 14 by September 2026, while the company expects its data-center portfolio to generate about $1 billion in calendar 2026 revenues. Future Gen6 switch and retimer contributions could provide an additional growth catalyst from 2027 onward.
Aerospace and defense remains another important growth avenue, representing 16.7% of June-quarter revenues. Microchip's business has expanded from roughly $600 million in 2022 to approximately $1 billion, supported by defense inventory rebuilding and multiyear demand. Its radiation-tolerant, radiation-hardened and FPGA products address space and defense applications requiring high reliability, long lifecycles and stringent performance requirements.
Improving bookings, factory utilization and expense discipline are supporting operating leverage as Microchip's recovery progresses. Management reported its strongest bookings quarter in roughly four years and expects fiscal second-quarter 2027 gross margins of 66-67% and operating margins of 38.5-39.5%. The pending Hailo acquisition could accelerate Microchip's edge-AI roadmap while adding complementary technology and engineering capabilities.
However, external manufacturing dependence, China exposure and elevated leverage remain important risks. Microchip sources approximately 65% of wafers externally, creating potential bottlenecks if AI-driven demand tightens foundry and assembly capacity. China represents roughly 17-18% of revenue and faces increasing local competition. Meanwhile, net debt was 2.85 times adjusted EBITDA, limiting flexibility for buybacks and larger acquisitions.
For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Microchip expects net sales between $1.589 billion and $1.618 billion, which suggests sequential growth of 7-9%, with the midpoint implying approximately 40.6% year-over-year growth. The company expects non-GAAP earnings of 91-95 cents per share. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MCHP's second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 162.8%. Estimates have remained unchanged for the past 30 days.

ADI has the stronger overall growth profile, supported by a broader recovery across industrial, automotive and communications markets, accelerating AI infrastructure demand and stronger upward revisions to earnings estimates. While MCHP offers significant recovery potential, its higher external manufacturing dependence, China exposure and leverage create additional execution risks. Build Smarter, More Resilient 48V Power Systems with Energy-Aware Digital Power Monitoring from Microchip
Microchip Technology Inc.
Microchip Technology Inc.
New 65V digital power monitors help designers track accumulated energy data to improve system response in applications that also depend on higher levels of measurement headroom and spike protection
CHANDLER, Ariz., Sept. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- As automotive, AI/data center, networking and industrial systems quickly migrate toward 48V power architectures to improve efficiency and support higher power demands, designers need more than visibility into instantaneous voltage and current conditions. They need systems that understand energy use over time and can respond intelligently to changing power conditions. Microchip Technology (Nasdaq: MCHP) today announced the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors that combine accumulated power-measurement insights with the necessary high-voltage measurement headroom and transient spike protection capabilities to help make 48V power architectures more efficient and resilient.
The move to 48V power architectures demands that digital power monitors have an additional operational margin of up-to-65V measurement and 75V of spike protection to ensure transient survivability. The PAC1761 and PAC1861 devices add to these capabilities the intelligence to understand and react in real time to energy usage dynamics based on accumulated power measurement data.
"The industry conversation is shifting from measuring power at a single point in time to understanding and responding to energy behavior across an entire system and its lifecycle," said Keith Pazul, vice president of Microchip's mixed-signal linear business unit. "The PAC1761 and PAC1861 families are designed to help customers build better performing and more reliable 48V systems that can measure instantaneous conditions and understand energy consumption and availability over time. These scalable, low-power solutions reduce monitoring overhead and include pin-compatible package options that improve source flexibility while reducing design risk."
Microchip's digital power monitoring devices feature programmable alerts for voltage, current and power excursions, step-limit detection to identify sudden load changes, and configurable accumulated-energy thresholds that enable proactive system management based on both instantaneous and long-term power behavior.
Target applications include automotive, AI/data center, networking, industrial, server, telecom/Power over Ethernet (PoE) and 48V power distribution systems. The 12-bit PAC1761 and 16-bit PAC1861 options are available in VDFN-8 (similar to SOT23-8), VDFN-10 and MSOP-10 packages including automotive-orderable variants. Pin-compatible options can reduce redesign risk, shorten qualification cycles and give customers flexibility to move between devices as requirements, availability, cost or performance change.
Development support includes evaluation board EV12R33A, a Python Command Line Interface (CLI) with library, Linux® driver and generic C library with multiple MCU code examples.
Products in the PAC1761 and PAC1861 families are available now starting at $0.56 each in 10,000-unit quantities for the PAC1761T-3E/E3 and PAC1861T-1E/3P, both in the MSOP-10 package. The price of the evaluation board EV12R33A is $49.00. You can purchase directly from Microchip or contact a Microchip sales representative or authorized worldwide distributor.

facts.text: Microchip expanded its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with LAN8679, LAN8680 transceivers and LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family for automotive, industrial, robotics and aerospace applications.
Microchip Technology's share price fell 15.06% over the past 90 days despite a 14.85% year-to-date return.
Microchip Technology stock closed at EUR 72.34 on October 2, 2026, and remained unchanged at the same price during weekend trading on October 4, 2026.
Microchip expanded its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with LAN8679, LAN8680 transceivers and LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family for automotive, industrial, robotics and aerospace applications.

Microchip Technology expanded its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with LAN8679, LAN8680 PMD transceivers, and LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family for automotive, industrial, robotics, and aerospace applications.
Microchip's 10BASE-T1S portfolio targets a $4-billion market across automotive, aerospace, robotics, industrial vehicles, and building controls.
Industrial revenues represented 32.2% of Microchip's Q1 fiscal 2027 revenues, up 24.3% YoY.
Automotive revenues accounted for 15% of Microchip's Q1 fiscal 2027 revenues, up 29.3% YoY.
Microchip's stock has appreciated 22% year to date, trading at a trailing P/B multiple of 6.55.
Zacks Consensus Estimate for Microchip's fiscal 2027 earnings is $3.63 per share, up 15.6% over the past 30 days.

Microchip Technology announced expansion of its 10BASE-T1S Single Pair Ethernet portfolio with new transceivers and endpoint devices, including LAN8679, LAN8680 transceivers and LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family.
The new products meet AEC-Q100 automotive qualification requirements and ISO 26262 functional safety standards, simplifying wiring and enabling flexible edge connectivity.
Microchip Technology's stock jumped 1.9% after the announcement, closing at $79.42.
Microchip Technology's shares have had 24 moves greater than 5% over the last year.
Microchip launched PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V digital power monitors for 48V power applications to measure energy use and withstand voltage spikes.
Microchip's stock is up 22.1% since the beginning of the year, trading 22.8% below its 52-week high of $102.92 from May 2026.
Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Microchip shares 5 years ago would now have $1,038.
Microchip expanded its 10BASE-T1S portfolio with LAN8679 and LAN8680 transceivers and LAN8660X/1X/2X endpoint family for automotive and industrial applications.

Microchip Technology announced PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors for 48V power architectures, offering real-time energy usage monitoring and transient spike protection.
PAC1761 and PAC1861 devices provide programmable alerts for voltage, current, and power excursions, step-limit detection, and configurable accumulated-energy thresholds.
Target applications include automotive, AI/data center, networking, industrial, server, telecom, and 48V power distribution systems.
Products available now starting at $0.56 each in 10,000-unit quantities for PAC1761T-3E/E3 and PAC1861T-1E/3P models.
Evaluation board EV12R33A is available for $49.00.
Microchip Technology's net sales breakdown: mixed-signal microcontrollers (51.1%), interface and analogue products (26.3%), other (22.6%).
Microchip Technology's geographic sales distribution: Americas (30.2%), Asia (49.9%), Europe (19.9%).
Microchip Technology stock fell 1.50 percent to USD 74.40 on Nasdaq on September 24, 2026
Microchip's fiscal Q1 2027 adjusted EPS reached USD 0.76, exceeding the USD 0.70 consensus
Microchip's fiscal Q1 2027 revenue was USD 1.48 billion, up 38% YoY and 13.2% sequentially
25 analysts have an average 12-month target of USD 107.84 with 20 Buy ratings
Microchip's market cap is USD 40.4 billion with a 52-week range of USD 48.52-105.91
Microchip announced PAC1761 and PAC1861 families of 65V energy-aware digital power monitors for 48V power architectures, offering accumulated energy data tracking and spike protection.
Microchip Technology completed its acquisition of Hailo on September 21, 2026, according to a press release.
Microchip Technology stock traded above its 52-week low but below its 52-week high as of September 18, 2026.
Microchip Technology's revenue in fiscal 2026 is meaningfully higher than in fiscal 2024, with gross margins several percentage points above historical averages.
Microchip Technology stock closed at USD 71.48 on Nasdaq on September 14, 2026, down 3.7% from prior close.
Microchip Technology's GF Value fair-value estimate was USD 66.03, implying the stock was 8.3% overvalued.
Microchip Technology reported Q3 revenue of USD 462.1 million, up 13.9% QoQ and 3.3% YoY.
Microchip Technology had an operating loss of USD 7.17 million for the quarter, a 42.4% reduction from prior quarter.
Microchip Technology's gross margin for the quarter was 15.6%, within its guidance range of 14.0-16.0%.
Microchip Technology guided next quarter revenue between USD 445.0 million and USD 485.0 million.
Microchip Technology's consensus price target is USD 98.67, representing 38.0% upside from current price.
